# PLAN — iteration 2
## Current state assessment
Iteration 1 passed behavior and timing but was rejected because it kept the incumbent at 16 LUTs and 34 FFs. The current design has 16 CRC state FFs and 16 registered output CRC FFs; its output slot and CRC update must retain one-byte-per-cycle throughput, synchronous reset priority, and stall stability.

## Hypothesis
Using the registered output CRC as the running frame state can remove the separate 16-bit `frame_crc` register and reduce FF usage, while keeping the same CRC value available for each accepted byte.

## Instruction for generator
In `crc16_stream_core`, remove `frame_crc` and use `out_crc_reg` as the input state to `crc16_update` on each accepted byte; after `in_last`, select `16'hFFFF` as the next update seed instead of storing a separate frame state. Preserve the existing output register, valid/ready replacement and stall behavior, and synchronous reset semantics; ensure a stalled output remains stable while the next update uses the reset frame seed when the preceding accepted byte had `in_last=1`. Keep `// @latency 1` on the top and verify the complete unit against the frozen integration testbench and routed gates.
